summary: Reproduced the DFLASH/DSPARK page_size=1 req_to_token headroom mismatch (21 slots versus a 34-slot decode reserve), widened DFLASH-family rows at every page size, and added a fail-fast bound check before DFLASH allocation.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction on the recorded base: DFLASH and DSPARK page_size=1 each produced headroom 21 below reserve 34; page_size=16 and non-spec boundary cases passed.
Passing-after sizing invariants for DSPARK/DFLASH at page size 1, DFLASH alignment at page size 16, unchanged non-spec behavior, explicit overflow rejection, and no regression to UNO sizing.
Patch whitespace plus repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, and registered-test metadata checks.
Confirmed the assigned single AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 GPU was visible; no GPU workload was needed or run for this pure sizing/bookkeeping defect.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned gfx950 GPU was enumerated with rocm-smi, but the issue-specific reproduction and regression are CPU-only. No compatible DFLASH/DSPARK model weights were available.

remaining_limitations: No live DFLASH/DSPARK server reproduction was run because compatible target and draft model weights were not provided.
The reported 4x B200 production workload, cross-request corruption, and delayed idle leak were not reproduced on the assigned single gfx950 GPU.
The tests establish the exact sizing mismatch, aligned boundary behavior, and fail-fast allocation bound, but do not make semantic-accuracy or distributed-workload claims.
